name: Overnight chia pudding, almond milk
method: Mix the chia seeds, almond milk and frozen berries in a jar the night before.
Chill overnight so the chia swells and thickens it.
In the morning, stir through the yoghurt and a pinch of salt.

name: Cottage cheese, flax & walnut bowl

ingredients.text: Small handful berries (~20g; frozen is fine)
Splash of cream or unsweetened almond milk, to loosen

method: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl.
Stir through the flaxseed and cinnamon.
Scatter the walnuts and berries on top.
Loosen with a splash of cream if it's too thick.

name: Soft-boiled eggs with buttered greens
method: Soft-boil the eggs, about 6 min from a simmering pot, then peel.
Wilt the greens in butter in a small pan, about 2 min for spinach or a little longer for silverbeet.
Season and serve together.

name: Soft-boiled eggs with avocado

ingredients.text: 1 avocado (if in season; otherwise extra eggs and a little feta)

method: Boil the eggs for 6–7 min.
Peel and halve them over sliced avocado.
Scatter the seeds, drizzle with oil and season.

name: Scrambled eggs with spinach, feta & cherry tomatoes
method: Melt the butter in a pan over a medium-low heat.
Add the beaten eggs and stir gently as they start to set.
Fold in the spinach so it wilts in the residual heat.
Crumble over the feta, add the halved cherry tomatoes and season.

name: Greek yoghurt with berries, chia & walnuts
method: Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl.
Stir through the chia seeds and cinnamon.
Top with the berries and crushed walnuts.

name: Bacon, spinach & mushroom mini-quiches

ingredients.text: 200g cheddar, grated (grate your own; pre-grated runs higher carb)

method: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Fry the bacon and mushrooms, then wilt the spinach in the same pan.
Whisk the eggs, cream, cheese, salt and pepper.
Stir in the fillings and divide between two 12-cup silicone trays (24 cups).
Bake 20–22 min until set.
Serve 2–3 per person, warmed.
tip: Makes 24. Keeps 4–5 days in the fridge and freezes well. For lunch, serve 2–3 with a leafy salad, cucumber, olives and pumpkin seeds dressed with olive oil, lemon and salt.

name: Almond-crust bacon & spinach quiche
method: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Rub the almond flour, cold butter, egg and salt together into a crust.
Press it into a fluted flan pan and blind-bake 10 min.
Soften the bacon, mushrooms, spring onions and spinach in one pan.
Whisk the eggs, cream, cheese, salt and pepper, then fold in the cooked fillings.
Pour into the crust and bake 30–35 min until just set.
tip: Cuts into 6 slices; a good savoury breakfast or a top-up when a day runs light.

name: Tuna & avocado lettuce boats
method: Mix the tuna, avocado and cucumber.
Dress with a squeeze of lemon, a drizzle of olive oil, salt and pepper.
Spoon into the lettuce leaves and eat like tacos.

name: Egg salad plate
method: Peel and chop the hard-boiled eggs.
Mix with the mayonnaise, cucumber and mustard.
Season and serve with the olives alongside.

name: Deli plate: prosciutto, cheese & olives

ingredients.text: A few cubes or slices of cheese

method: Arrange everything on a plate.
Drizzle the tomatoes and cucumber with olive oil and crack pepper over.
tip: Keeps well, so this is a good late-week lunch.

name: Smoked salmon, cream cheese & cucumber plate

ingredients.text: 1/3 cucumber, sliced into rounds or batons

method: Lay the smoked salmon out with a dollop of cream cheese and the cucumber alongside.
Squeeze lemon over, crack pepper and scatter the capers.
Roll the salmon around the cream cheese and cucumber, or build little stacks.
tip: Smoked salmon keeps well, so this is a good late-week lunch.

name: Chicken & avocado salad bowl
method: Pile the greens, cucumber, avocado and chicken into two bowls.
Dress with olive oil, lemon and salt.
Scatter the seeds over.

name: Bacon & cheese omelette
method: Fry the chopped bacon in the pan first.
Pour the beaten eggs over.
As it sets, scatter the cheese and spinach on.
Fold and slide out.

name: Steak with sauteed mushrooms & rocket
method: Season the steak well.
Sear in a hot pan with a little oil, about 3–4 min a side for medium-rare, then rest it.
In the same pan, add butter, the mushrooms and garlic and cook until golden, about 5 min.
Pile the rocket on the plate and sit the sliced steak and mushrooms on top so the rocket wilts a little.
tip: Beef keeps a few days in the fridge if you don't get to it straight away.

name: Chicken thigh traybake with broccoli & lemon
method: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Toss the broccoli, garlic and herbs in oil on a tray.
Sit the chicken thighs on top and season the skin.
Roast about 30 min until the skin is crisp and the broccoli edges catch.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon.
tip: Swap the broccoli for sliced fennel and a few olives for a change. Chicken holds to the end of the week, or freezes if you won't get to it.

name: Lamb chops with braised cabbage & mustard cream
method: Sear the lamb chops in butter, about 3–4 min a side for medium-rare, then rest.
In the same pan, soften the garlic.
Add the cabbage with a splash of water and cook until just tender, 6–8 min.
Stir through the cream and mustard and season.
Sit the lamb on top to serve.

name: Lamb chops with roast cauliflower & courgette

ingredients.text: 6–8 lamb loin chops or cutlets (3–4 each)

method: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Toss the cauliflower and courgette in oil, garlic and rosemary on a tray and roast 15 min.
Meanwhile, sear the chops in a hot pan with butter, about 2–3 min a side for pink.
Rest the chops and serve over the roast veg with lemon squeezed over.
tip: Or roast the chops on the tray for the veg's last 12–15 min.

name: Baked white fish with garlic-butter greens

ingredients.text: 1 white fish fillet (tarakihi, hoki or similar, ~150g)

method: Bake the fish about 10 min at 200°C, or pan-fry 3–4 min a side, until just cooked through.
Meanwhile, wilt the garlic and silverbeet in butter.
Squeeze lemon over both to serve.
tip: No silverbeet? Use baby spinach and add it at the end; it wilts in under a minute.

name: One-pan beef mince stir-fry

ingredients.text: A sprinkle of seeds, to finish

method: Brown the mince in a hot pan, then push it aside.
Fry the garlic and ginger for 30 sec.
Add the courgette, mushroom and capsicum and stir-fry until tender.
Combine everything, splash in the tamari and season.
Scatter the seeds over to serve.
tip: Drop the capsicum for about 3g less net carbs per serve.

name: Pan-seared salmon, lemon butter & greens

ingredients.text: 150g greens: broccolini, silverbeet or baby spinach

method: Sear the salmon skin-side down in a little butter, about 4 min.
Flip for about 2 min more until just cooked, then lift out and rest.
In the same pan, melt more butter with the garlic.
Wilt the greens (a splash of water helps broccolini) and squeeze in lemon.
Spoon the lemon butter over the salmon.
tip: Cook this early in the week; fresh fish won't keep.

name: Sheet-pan salmon with fennel & courgette
method: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Toss the fennel and courgette in oil on a lined tray and roast 10 min.
Lay the salmon on top, dot with butter, season and add lemon slices.
Roast another 12–15 min until the salmon just flakes.
Squeeze lemon over and scatter seeds to serve.
tip: Fennel stands in for asparagus in winter; use asparagus when it's in season.

name: Berries, mascarpone (or cream) & dark chocolate

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp mascarpone (~30g), or 2 tbsp cream shaken until thick

method: Spoon the mascarpone (or shaken cream) over the defrosted berries.
Grate the dark chocolate on top.
tip: A drop of vanilla and a few crushed macadamias work in place of the chocolate.

name: Walnut & dark chocolate bites
method: Plate the walnuts with a square of dark chocolate.
tip: A small handful of macadamias works just as well as the walnuts.

name: Fudgy tahini-sesame slice

ingredients.text: 250g hulled tahini (stir well first; the oil separates)
50g butter, melted (brown it for deeper flavour if you like)
30g sesame seeds, lightly toasted (half folded in, half for the top)
A good pinch of flaky salt

method: Heat the oven to 165°C and line a small, deep 18cm tin or a loaf tin.
Beat the tahini, melted butter, erythritol, eggs and vanilla until smooth and glossy.
Fold in the almond flour, coconut, salt and half the sesame to a thick, fudgy paste.
Press into the tin so the bar stays tall, smooth the top and scatter the rest of the sesame.
Bake 14–18 min, pulling it while the centre is still soft; underbaked is fudgy.
Cool, then chill 1–2 hours to set and cut it cold.
If using chocolate, spread the melted chocolate over the cooled slice and chill again.
tip: Makes about 10 thick bars; keep them in the fridge. Hulled tahini keeps a bar near 2g net (1.5g without the chocolate); unhulled tahini can push it to about 5g, so check the label.

name: Cheese, olives & macadamias
method: Plate and eat.

name: Whey protein shake
method: Shake the whey and liquid together in a bottle.
tip: About 25g protein per scoop.

name: Seed toast with smashed avocado & kimchi
method: Toast the seed loaf slices.
Mash the avocado with a squeeze of lemon, salt and pepper.
Spread the avocado on the toast.
Top with the kimchi and a drizzle of olive oil.
tip: Pick the seed bread with the fewest carbs per slice, or bake the seed loaf in Extras. Add a soft-boiled egg on the side if you want it more filling; it adds well under 1g net.

name: Garlic mushrooms & asparagus on seed toast

ingredients.text: 3 asparagus spears (~60g), woody ends snapped off

method: Melt the butter in a frying pan over a medium-high heat.
Fry the mushrooms and asparagus for about 5 min until golden.
Add the garlic and thyme for the last minute, then season.
Toast the seed loaf slice.
Pile the mushrooms and asparagus on the toast and finish with the parmesan.
tip: Pick the seed bread with the fewest carbs per slice, or bake the seed loaf in Extras. No asparagus? Use a handful of baby spinach, wilted in the pan at the end.

name: Warm flax & coconut porridge

ingredients.text: 40g full-fat unsweetened Greek yoghurt, to top

method: Stir the flaxseed, coconut, almond flour, cinnamon and salt into 120 ml water in a small pan.
Simmer, stirring, for 2–3 min until it thickens.
Take it off the heat and stir in the cream.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the yoghurt.
tip: It keeps thickening as it sits; loosen with a splash more water or cream.

name: Bacon, avocado & tomato plate
method: Fry the bacon in a dry pan until crisp, then lift it out.
Put the tomatoes in the bacon fat, cut side down, for 2 min until they soften.
Plate the rocket, avocado and tomatoes.
Add the bacon, then finish with lemon, olive oil and pepper.
tip: Add a slice of low-carb seed toast for about 2g more net.

name: Fresh mozzarella, tomato & rocket plate

ingredients.text: 1 ball fresh mozzarella or buffalo mozzarella (~100g), torn

method: Scatter the rocket on a plate.
Add the torn mozzarella and halved tomatoes.
Tear the basil over.
Finish with plenty of olive oil, flaky salt and pepper.
tip: Take the mozzarella out of the fridge 20 min before; it tastes better at room temperature.

name: Pork & kimchi lettuce cups

ingredients.text: Few slices cucumber, cut into sticks (~40g)

method: Fry the pork mince in a little oil over a high heat, breaking it up, for 5–6 min until browned.
Stir in the kimchi for 1 min and season with salt.
Take off the heat and stir through most of the spring onion.
Spoon into the lettuce leaves, add cucumber sticks and the rest of the spring onion, and eat like tacos.
tip: Keep a spoonful of the kimchi back and add it cold on top for extra crunch.

name: Garlic butter prawns with courgette ribbons
method: Peel the courgette into long ribbons with a vegetable peeler.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and add the garlic and chilli for 30 sec.
Add the prawns and cook 1–2 min a side until pink all through; lift them out.
Toss the courgette ribbons in the garlic butter for 1–2 min until just soft.
Return the prawns, add lemon, parsley and salt, and serve.
tip: Cook this early in the week; fresh prawns won't keep. Frozen raw prawns work too; thaw them in the fridge first.

name: Pork scotch steak with creamed spinach
method: Take the pork out of the fridge 20 min before and season it well.
Fry it in a hot pan with the butter, 4–5 min a side until just cooked through, then rest it on a warm plate.
In the same pan, soften the garlic for 30 sec.
Add the spinach and stir until wilted.
Pour in the cream with the nutmeg and bubble for 1–2 min until it coats the spinach.
Slice the pork and serve it on the creamed spinach.
tip: Scotch (shoulder) steak stays juicy because it's marbled; a pork loin chop works too but dries out faster. Silverbeet works in place of spinach; cook it a little longer.

name: Dark chocolate mousse
method: Melt the chocolate with 3 tbsp of the cream in a bowl over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring until smooth.
Take it off the heat, stir in the vanilla and salt, and let it cool for 5 min.
Whisk the rest of the cream to soft peaks.
Fold the chocolate into the cream in two goes until no streaks remain.
Spoon into two small glasses and chill for at least 1 hour.
tip: Makes 2; the second keeps 2 days in the fridge, covered. It's bittersweet; a few raspberries on top add about 1g net.

name: Frozen yoghurt berry bark
method: Line a small tray or container with baking paper.
Stir the vanilla into the yoghurt.
Spread the yoghurt about 1cm thick on the paper.
Scatter over the berries, chocolate and pumpkin seeds and press them in lightly.
Freeze for at least 3 hours until firm.
Break into 6 pieces and keep them in a container in the freezer.
tip: Let a piece sit 5 min out of the freezer before eating so it softens a little.

name: Seed loaf
method: Heat the oven to 160°C and line a 900g (about 22 × 11cm) loaf tin with baking paper.
Whisk the eggs, olive oil and salt in a large bowl.
Stir in all the seeds, the flaxseed and the almond flour until every seed is coated.
Leave it 10 min so the flaxseed thickens the mix.
Press it firmly into the tin and smooth the top.
Bake for about 60 min, until firm and golden.
Cool 10 min in the tin, then lift it out onto a rack.
Cool completely before cutting into 16 slices.
tip: Keeps 5 days in the fridge. Slice before freezing and toast slices straight from frozen.

name: Kimchi devilled eggs
method: Hard-boil the eggs, about 9 min from a simmering pot, then cool in cold water and peel.
Halve them and scoop the yolks into a bowl.
Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, kimchi and a pinch of salt.
Spoon the filling back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika.
tip: Boil a few extra eggs at the start of the week; they keep peeled in the fridge for 3–4 days.
